name: Razor Hill Watchtower
summary: Furl Scornbrow watches Durotar from the Razor Hill Watchtower. From its red stone bluffs, he keeps an eye on the plains and coast, guarding the settlement below.

sections.title: Eyes Over Durotar
sections.body: The Razor Hill Watchtower rises above Razor Hill and the canyons around it. Thick timber and iron framing hold the outpost together. Durotar faces threats from Kul Tiras marines along the eastern shore, quilboar raiders across the scrublands, and Burning Blade cultists in nearby crags. From the ridgeline, a lookout can spot warbands, smoke signals, and incursions before they reach the settlement gates.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Razor Hill Watchtower?
faq.answer: The Razor Hill Watchtower is the main lookout for Razor Hill and central Durotar. Its height lets scouts watch the trails, spot hostile beasts, and see troop movements from nearby Alliance camps or centaur raiding parties.
Furl Scornbrow, an aging orc, watches for invaders and sounds his signal horn when needed. As Durotar has grown more settled, he has also taken to making bags for young adventurers.

faq.q: What threats can be seen from up here?
faq.answer: Scouts primarily watch for aggressive quilboar of the Razormane tribes, human infiltrators from Tiragarde Keep along the eastern coast, and wild beasts in the dry valleys.

angles.text: For young warriors and scouts leaving the Valley of Trials, the watchtower is a reassuring landmark of the fledgling Horde’s safety and strength.
The watchtower’s high, unobstructed vantage point is ideal for spotters tracking quarry and watching beast movements across Durotar.
